summary: PASS. git-branch.ts is well-architected with consistent no-throw semantics and '-' prefix injection guards on createBranch() and switchBranch(). Test coverage is thorough (19 tests, 265 lines) including security tests for the prefix guard, detached HEAD, fallback branch detection, and remote-tracking branch differentiation. The path-traversal risk in branchExists() is honestly documented in JSDoc and flagged for a future cleanup WP. No blocking issues.

comments.note: Implementation quality is high. createBranch() and switchBranch() both include a '-' prefix guard returning exitCode 128 before invoking git — this prevents flag injection and is exercised by dedicated tests. The pattern is consistent and well-tested.

[documentation-forward] branchExists() in src/git/git-branch.ts contains an explicit @remarks callout about path-traversal risk when untrusted input is passed (branchName='../config' can resolve to unintended refs). The JSDoc note is correct and the risk is documented, but the Documentation agent should ensure this warning is surfaced in any public API docs or consumer-facing documentation, not just inline JSDoc.

The duplicate-branch test assertion (exitCode !== 0 || stderr.length > 0) is slightly loose — exitCode !== 0 alone would be sufficient since git always exits non-zero for duplicate branch creation. Not blocking, but worth noting for future test maintenance.
